records.sourceLabel: SSRN exact paper record located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The paper constructs a labelled dataset of 2,082 Mafia-connected Italian firms from judicial evidence and applies gradient-boosted classification to financial-statement information. The abstract reports hold-out performance of 75.8% AUC and 90.4% precision, using accounting patterns to identify criminal connections.
records.note: Parallel Search fetched the exact SSRN title/authors/DOI record and located the direct 50-page PDF. The synopsis is abstract_only; the full-text locator is stored separately in retrieval_coverage.csv. No verbatim abstract or model-derived scientific decision is persisted here.

records.sourceLabel: American Economic Association publisher record located with Parallel Search
records.synopsis: The article studies firm-level effects of Mafia infiltration by combining investigative records with panel data on governance and balance sheets. It reports that targeted firms tend to be young and less efficient and that infiltration is associated with higher revenues without proportional input growth, alongside worsening financial conditions and eventual market exit.
records.note: Parallel Search located and fetched the exact AEA DOI/title/authors publisher record. The synopsis uses the verified publisher abstract only (abstract_only); the existing retrieval ledger already records the publisher full-text PDF. No abstract text is persisted here.

records.sourceLabel: RePEc/CEPR abstract record located with Parallel Search

records.synopsis: The working paper exploits variation in firms’ exposure to Covid-19 closure days as a shock to revenues and financial conditions to estimate whether distress raises Mafia infiltration risk. It reports that worsening financial conditions increased infiltration likelihood, while government support partly offset the effect; heterogeneity is consistent with a role for Mafia lending when firms face temporary debt-repayment difficulties.

records.synopsis: The paper studies whether credit rationing makes distressed firms more vulnerable to organised-crime infiltration. Using confidential UIF mapping of firms potentially connected to organised crime and firm-level data for the universe of Italian companies over 2001–2020, it compares firms downgraded to substandard credit risk with firms not downgraded in the same year and reports a persistent contraction in credit together with a subsequent increase in infiltration risk.
